headline: Use {arm:beta}, provisionally: of the two arms inside both bars it gets the total right more often, but this run cannot separate it from the cheaper {arm:gamma}.
lede: {arm:beta} leads {arm:gamma} by {aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.change|pts} points on the right total, an interval that reaches below zero, while {arm:alpha}, the strongest answerer, misses both bars. If a larger run shows the lead is noise, {arm:gamma}, cheaper and faster, becomes the pick.
flag: Only the cost and turn-time bars were set in advance. Nothing declared how often an arm must get the total right, or what a point of it is worth.

caveats.material_if: the lead of the arm picked shrinks on fresh cases, as the best of a few tends to; then the cheaper and faster arm is the pick
the owner values the cheaper arm's lower cost or turn time inside the bars, or needs a minimum answer rate; either ranks the two arms inside the bars differently from answering alone

a paired read over the shared cases moves the beta-against-gamma verdict; today's corrected pair interval already reaches below zero, so pairing could only firm up or dissolve the lead, not reverse the bar verdicts
the queued backlog differed between arms' runs; the extractor trades thoroughness for speed under backlog, so it would move both turn time and answer rate, the two things this call rests on
a different grader tolerance or key scored one arm's runs, moving its answer rate with no change in what it extracted
a different OCR build fed one arm's runs, so a missed total was never legible to it
a different model played the user for one arm's runs
the simulated user ran with a different output cap or reasoning budget for one arm's runs
the simulated user's calls were sent with different request settings for one arm's runs
one arm saw cleaner scans than another
one arm saw documents in a language its field labels don't match
handwritten annotation differed between arms' documents
the adjudicated template graded against differed between arms' runs
a payment hold was in force from the first turn for one arm and not another
operator corrections arrived at different points for different arms
supervisor sign-off differed between arms' runs, changing what the goal check reads

caveats.id: unreported:orchestration_ms (llm_ms, tool_ms were not measured, so the parts cannot account for the whole.)
caveats.material_if: a fix needs to know which part of the turn is slow; the bar reads whole-turn time, which is measured, so the call does not rest on the parts

decision.text: Use {arm:beta}. It clears both bars and gets the total right in {pass_rate.beta|pct} of trials, the best of the arms that clear them; its lead over {arm:gamma} is a point estimate, not a separated result.

{arm:alpha} costs {scoreboard.alpha.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} against a bar of {criteria.answers/bar/cost_usd.threshold|usd_per_1k}, and misses the turn-time bar too, each by its whole interval. Its answer lead over {arm:beta} is not separated either ({aspects.answers.pair.alpha.beta.interval|interval} points).
{arm:gamma} is cheaper and faster, but both arms already sit inside the bars, so its saving buys nothing the question asks for; it gets the total right in {pass_rate.gamma|pct} of trials.

Turn time is {arm:beta}'s nearest line: {weakest.margin} under the bar on its mean, and its p95 reaches {measure.total_ms.beta.p95}. A run of today's size would read {arm:gamma} ahead {settle.beta.gamma.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.wrong_side|pct} of the time, if the true gap equals today's.

A larger run of {arm:beta} and {arm:gamma} on the same fresh cases: about {settle.beta.gamma.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.cases_needed_80|int} trials per arm separates them four times in five if the gap is real, fewer when read paired.

claims.text: {arm:alpha} misses both bars by its whole interval; {arm:beta} and {arm:gamma} clear both.

evidence.caption: Cost per 1,000 replies; the dashed line is the declared cost bar.

claims.text: Inside the bars, {arm:beta} gets the total right more often than {arm:gamma}, but the gap of {aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.change|pts} points has a corrected interval reaching below zero ({aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.interval|interval}).

evidence.caption: Share of trials with the right total, each arm's own interval; the gap in the sentence is corrected across the three pairs.

claims.text: Separating {arm:beta} from {arm:gamma} takes about {settle.beta.gamma.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.cases_needed_80|int} trials per arm, against {scoreboard.beta.ran|int} each today.

evidence.caption: Trials run, passed and failed for the two arms inside the bars.

claims.text: Every failure is a wrong total: all {n_candidates|words} arms cite the policy in every trial.

evidence.caption: Both checks per arm as a share of trials, with intervals.

explore.outcome: Lowering the bar under {scoreboard.beta.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} leaves {arm:gamma} the only arm inside. Raising it to {scoreboard.alpha.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} does not admit {arm:alpha} alone, since it also misses the turn-time bar.

A bar inside {arm:beta}'s interval ({aspects.answers.bar.total_ms.beta.interval|interval}) or below it leaves {arm:gamma} the only arm inside. {arm:alpha} needs a bar above {aspects.answers.bar.total_ms.alpha.interval|interval}.

A floor between {pass_rate.gamma|pct} and {pass_rate.beta|pct} leaves {arm:beta} the only arm inside the bars that meets it; a floor above {pass_rate.beta|pct} leaves none, since {arm:alpha} misses both bars.

method.text: {cases|int} cases, each run {repeats|int} times per arm; intervals are over cases, not trials.
A trial passes when the reply's total matches the case total. Citing the policy is checked too, and every arm passes it every time.

Each arm's rate carries its own interval at {spread.beta.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.level}. Differences between two arms are corrected across the three pairs, read at {aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.confidence}.

The question asks which arm answers within the cost and turn-time bars, so both bars rule options out here. The pipeline reads bars as warnings and lists all three arms as surviving; this report departs from that for this reason.
Spend per reply across all roles, which equals production cost per reply for every arm.
No arm is a control; arms compare in pairs.
